title: The Bog Oak
text: A black oak trunk thousands of years old juts out of the peat like the prow of a sunken ship. The wood is hard as iron and dark as a starless night. Bog oak makes the finest bows in the world, the old bowyers say, and it is rarely found whole.

options.label: Dig the black trunk out of the peat, however long it takes.

outcomes.text: The black timber comes free, hard as iron and heavy as guilt.
The bog wants it back, and you along with it. It pulls with all its patient strength.

options.label: The cleverest carves a bow from it on the spot, before the bog can take it back.

outcomes.text: A fine black bow takes shape over a long afternoon. The whole time, the peat bubbles and sighs.

options.label: Leave it to the bog. It has kept the oak this long for a reason.

outcomes.text: As you turn away, the peat sighs and gives up a small thing it was keeping: a sliver of black wood, hard as iron, which the Leader binds to their weapon.
It will wait for you too, the bog seems to say. That night the Leader dreams of black water.

options.label: The one with a bow cuts a new stave from it, eager to see it sing.

outcomes.text: It takes all night, and the bog does not like it. Still, the new limbs are black and hard as iron.
